plan.notes: Source: the official 'Sample 4 Year Plan' table on the UC San Diego Computer Science and Engineering department's B.S. Computer Science page (https://cse.ucsd.edu/undergraduate/bs-computer-science, page header 'Updated August 13th, 2026'; '2026-2027 B.S. Computer Science Electives'; 'B.S. Computer Science Checklist (Fall 2026 Curriculum)'). The official UC San Diego General Catalog 2026-27 (https://catalog.ucsd.edu/curric/CSE-ug.html) states 'See the CSE website for a sample four-year plan of study,' making this the catalog-sanctioned official sequence. Course titles, unit values, and prerequisites are verbatim from the 2026-27 General Catalog course listings (catalog.ucsd.edu/courses/CSE.html, MATH.html, ECE.html, ECON.html, PHYS.html). Catalog year: 2026-2027 (the current General Catalog; all course pages read 'For course descriptions not found in the UC San Diego General Catalog 2026-27...'). Transcription method: manual, course-by-course transcription of the official 12-quarter (Fall/Winter/Spring x 4 years) sample sequence; prereqs simplified from the catalog's 'or' alternatives to the standard-track in-plan course. QUARTER SYSTEM: UCSD runs on quarters; 180 quarter units is the official bachelor's degree minimum. The catalog states the BS Computer Science program itself 'requires a total of 124 units for the BS computer science program (not including the general-education requirements)'. CAVEATS: (1) The official sample plan explicitly covers MAJOR requirements only ('These plans only include CSE major requirements'); college GE and university requirements vary across UCSD's eight colleges, so the remaining 56 units are modeled as 13 student-choice 'GE ELECTIVE' slots (4 units each) with choice_note guidance; plans.ucsd.edu publishes college-specific full plans. (2) The sample plan is written for the standard intro track (CSE 8A in Fall, CSE 11 in Winter); per official footnote *1, students with programming experience begin with CSE 11 in Fall and take CSE 12 + CSE 29 in Winter — documented in the Fall Y1 choice_note. (3) The official plan shows two 'Lower Division Elective (LDE)' cells in Year 1; modeled as 2-unit seminar-style choice slots each. Official footnote *2 states that taking CSE 8A alone fulfills the 4-unit LDE requirement, so the sample sequence as modeled totals 128 major units vs the catalog's 124-unit program minimum. (4) Upper-division elective slots (Systems / Theory-Abstraction / Applications / Open CSE) are student-choice from the official 2026-2027 tagged lists; each course may count toward only one tag (12 units each tag + 24 open = 60 elective units). (5) The Fall 2026 curriculum replaced CSE 15L (2 units) with CSE 29 (4 units) as the lab option; all catalog unit values verified above. external_prereqs is empty: every listed prereq names a course in this plan.

courses.choice_note: Official plan footnote *1: students with no programming experience begin with the two-course sequence CSE 8A (then CSE 11 in Winter). Students with programming experience begin with CSE 11 in Fall (then take CSE 12 and CSE 29 in Winter). Either option is 4 units. CSE 8A title: 'Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving I'; CSE 11 title: 'Introduction to Programming and Computational Problem-Solving: Accelerated Pace'.
